notes.summary: Draft sufficient-condition solution on P¹×P¹ with a genuine logarithmic-divisor model reference, a non-Gauduchon background, and factorized continuous density. Proves singleton supports on the full space C(X), an explicitly normalized weighted non-pluripolar current, and approximation independence under uniform convergence of residual forms with fixed divisor. Includes nonsmooth compact examples and an obstruction to unrestricted pole smoothing. Does not cover degenerate solution residuals or potential-only convergence.
notes.detailedSummary: Take theta=(a+lambda)omega_1+b(x)omega_2, with a,lambda>0 and smooth positive nonconstant b. An explicit obstacle calculation constructs an ordinary divisorial model reference phi~psi and proves the additional epsilon-envelope admissibility. For continuous F satisfying q exp(F)/(2b)=H(x)>0, put m=integral H omega_1, c=a/m and A=cH. A Green kernel constructs bounded continuous w with dd^c w=(A-a)omega_1. The genuine singular solution u=psi+w has continuous uniformly positive residual Omega=A omega_1+b omega_2 and non-pluripolar Monge-Ampere product Omega²=c exp(F)dV. The directly defined weight rho=1/(2ab) gives a continuous closed current Q=rho Omega and normalized probability nu=(A/a)dW. Potential perturbations force every full-space supporting probability to annihilate L=(1/A)Delta_1+(1/b)Delta_2. Spherical-harmonic separation and a proved heat-resolvent lemma identify nu as the unique invariant probability. For every smooth positive residual approximation converging uniformly to Omega, normalized classical adjoint probabilities and the actual weighted currents converge to nu and Q. The approximation class is nonempty and permits nonsymmetric perturbations. A Lipschitz example distinguishes nu from normalized Monge-Ampere volume by height moments 0 and 5/24. Raw smooth pole regularization instead produces divisor probability 1/5, disproving an unrestricted approximation assertion. The indispensable Bedford-Taylor and Gauduchon premises were checked at primary sources. Finite symbolic checks passed; the mathematical argument remains an unverified draft. This claims a complete restricted sufficient-condition answer, with its boundary retained.
notes.text:
Draft sufficient-condition theorem for a logarithmic divisor on a non-Gauduchon product surface

Claim and boundary. This is a complete proposed sufficient-condition answer to S07 in a specified genuinely singular-reference regime. The background and every smooth positive potential perturbation of it are non-Gauduchon. The reference has a divisorial pole and a degenerate residual on an open set. The solution has the same pole and may have only continuous residual coefficients. Supports are singleton on the FULL space C(X), including perturbations outside the special density family below. The weighted non-pluripolar current is defined directly, satisfies the operator identity, and is the limit for every approximation in the stated nonempty class. That class fixes the divisor and requires uniform convergence of residual forms. Potential convergence and arbitrary smoothing of the pole are insufficient; an explicit obstruction appears below.

1. Fully specified data and theorem

Let X=P¹_x×P¹_y. On each factor use the normalized Fubini-Study form omega_i=dd^c log(1+|z_i|²), with dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial, so integral omega_i=1. Pullbacks are understood. Set dW=omega_1 wedge omega_2, a probability volume. Let dV=q dW, where q is any smooth strictly positive function with integral q dW=1.

Choose a>0, lambda>0, and b in C^infinity(P¹_x), with min b>0 and b nonconstant. Define
  theta=(a+lambda)omega_1+b(x)omega_2,
  eta=a omega_1+b(x)omega_2.
Both forms are smooth strictly positive. In particular theta is semipositive and big: theta itself is a strictly positive theta-psh current, with potential zero.

Write x=[Z_0:Z_1], let D={Z_0=0}×P¹_y, and set
  psi=lambda log(|Z_0|²/(|Z_0|²+|Z_1|²)).
Use its canonical upper representative, equal to -infinity on D. Direct Poincare-Lelong calculation gives
  dd^c psi=lambda[D]-lambda omega_1,
  theta+dd^c psi=eta+lambda[D]>0.
Put K=a+lambda, R=a/lambda and
  C_*=K log(K/lambda)-a log(a/lambda).
On the chart Z_0 nonzero, with r²=|Z_1/Z_0|², define
  phi=0                                  for r²<=R,
  phi=a log r²+C_*-K log(1+r²)            for r²>=R,
and phi=-infinity on D. Section 2 proves that phi=P_theta[psi], sup phi=0, phi~psi, and P_theta[phi]=phi. For every epsilon with lambda/K<epsilon<1, P_(epsilon theta)(phi) is a genuine envelope.

Density hypothesis: F is continuous on X and
  q(x,y)exp(F(x,y))/(2b(x))=H(x)
for some continuous strictly positive H on P¹_x. No differentiability of H is assumed. Define
  m=integral H omega_1,
  c=a/m,
  A=cH.
Then A is continuous, uniformly positive, and integral A omega_1=a.

There is a bounded continuous real w on P¹_x, uniquely normalized by integral w omega_1=0, satisfying
  dd^c w=(A-a)omega_1.
Section 3 constructs it. Set u=psi+w; subtracting sup_X u is optional and changes none of the formulas. This is a genuine canonical theta-psh potential, u~phi, with continuous uniformly positive residual form
  Omega=eta+dd^c w=A(x)omega_1+b(x)omega_2.

For precisely the non-pluripolar products with smooth-background corrections specified in the task,
  <theta+dd^c u>=Omega,
  MA_ext_theta(u)=<(theta+dd^c u)²>=Omega²
                =2Ab dW=c exp(F)dV.
Thus c_phi(F)=c and B_phi(F)=log c.

Define the weight and weighted product DIRECTLY by
  rho=1/(2ab),
  Q=rho<theta+dd^c u>
   =[A/(2ab)]omega_1+[1/(2a)]omega_2.
This is ordinary multiplication of a continuous form by a smooth positive function, independently of the existence of supporting probabilities. It satisfies
  dQ=0, hence dd^c Q=0,
  integral rho Omega²=1.
The unique supporting probability is
  nu=rho Omega²=(A/a)dW=(H/m)dW.
Equivalently nu=c rho exp(F)dV. Without the chosen normalization, its formula is rho Omega²/integral rho Omega².

The weak linearization, on h in C^infinity(X,R), and its logarithmic version are
  D_u MA_ext(h)=2Omega wedge dd^c h,
  L_u h=2Omega wedge dd^c h/Omega²
       =(Delta_1 h)/A+(Delta_2 h)/b,
where dd^c_x h=(Delta_1 h)omega_1, and similarly in y. Mixed components of dd^c h have zero wedge with the diagonal Omega. The derivative is a signed measure with continuous density; L_u h is continuous. The operator identity is
  integral L_u h dnu
   =integral rho D_u MA_ext(h)
   =2 integral dd^c h wedge Q=0.
The measure adjoint has exactly one probability in its kernel, namely nu. Consequently A_phi(F)={nu}, using its full definition with every G in C(X). The displayed rho is also the unique normalized nonnegative integrable weight satisfying dd^c(rho Omega)=0.

Admissible approximation class: retain theta, eta, psi and D. Take ANY sequence w_j in C^infinity(X,R), normalized for example by integral w_j dW=0, such that
  Omega_j=eta+dd^c w_j>0,
  ||Omega_j-Omega||_(C^0 tensors, omega_1+omega_2) tends to zero.
No product symmetry is required of w_j. Put
  u_j=psi+w_j,
  F_j=log(Omega_j²/(c dV)).
These are genuine full-type solutions with fixed divisorial singularity, smooth strictly positive residual forms, smooth densities, and scalar c. Their densities converge uniformly to F. One may additionally require w_j to converge uniformly to w; the theorem remains true, and the explicit sequences below do so.

For each residual form let rho_j be its classical positive smooth adjoint, normalized by
  dd^c(rho_j Omega_j)=0,
  integral rho_j Omega_j²=1.
For EVERY sequence in this class,
  rho_j Omega_j² converges weakly to nu,
  rho_j Omega_j converges weakly as currents to Q,
  rho_j dW converges weakly as measures to rho dW.
This proves approximation independence of the actual weighted product, not just its supporting probability. Pointwise or strong convergence of rho_j is not asserted. The approximation class is nonempty.

2. Exact ordinary model reference and admissibility

For C>=0, psi is a candidate for E_C=P_theta(min(psi+C,0)), so E_C is genuine. The background and obstacle are invariant under the transitive PU(2) action on the second factor. Envelope equivariance makes E_C independent of y. For a function f(x), theta-psh is equivalent to K omega_1+dd^c f>=0 on the first factor, because the second block b omega_2 is strictly positive. Hence E_C is the pullback of the corresponding one-dimensional K omega_1 envelope.

That one-dimensional envelope is radial, by rotation invariance. For a radial K omega_1-psh function v, its total local potential
  g(s)=v+K log(1+exp s), s=log|z|²,
is convex. The obstacles imply
  g(s)<=K log(1+exp s),
  g(s)<=a log(1+exp s)+C.
The second bound forces every one-sided slope of g to be at most a: any larger slope would force eventual growth faster than as. At s_0=log(a/lambda), for s>=s_0,
  g(s)<=g(s_0)+a(s-s_0)
       <=K log(1+exp s_0)+a(s-s_0).
For s<=s_0 the first obstacle gives the desired upper bound. The maximal convex function is therefore the obstacle up to s_0 followed by its tangent line of slope a. Subtracting K log(1+exp s) produces the displayed phi.

Conversely phi is K omega_1-psh: its total radial potential is convex, slopes match at s_0, and its pole at D has coefficient lambda. There is no negative boundary current. It is <=0, and on X minus D
  0<=phi-psi<=C_*.
Inside the contact disk the difference is lambda log(1+r²); outside it is C_*-a log(1+r^(-2)). Thus phi is a candidate for E_C whenever C>=C_*. The upper bound proves E_C=phi for all such C, hence P_theta[psi]=phi.

The envelope P_theta[sigma] depends only on bounded singularity type. Indeed, if sigma<=tau+M, then
  min(sigma+C,0)<=min(tau+C+M,0).
Apply obstacle monotonicity and increasing limits; a reverse bounded comparison gives the reverse inequality. Since phi~psi, P_theta[phi]=P_theta[psi]=phi. The contact disk proves sup phi=0.

For lambda/K<epsilon<1,
  epsilon theta+dd^c psi
   =(epsilon K-lambda)omega_1+epsilon b omega_2+lambda[D]>0.
Since psi<=phi, psi is an actual epsilon theta-psh candidate below phi. Therefore P_(epsilon theta)(phi), between psi and phi, is a genuine canonical envelope.

Positive reference mass is explicit. On the contact disk the non-pluripolar horizontal residual is K omega_1; outside it is zero. Matching derivatives produce no boundary delta. Thus
  MA_ext_theta(phi)=2K b 1_{r²<R}dW,
with positive finite mass. Its horizontal residual mass is
  K integral_{r²<R}omega_1=KR/(1+R)=a.
This also exhibits reference-residual degeneracy on an open set.

Finally dd^c theta=(dd^c b) wedge omega_2 is nonzero: a smooth harmonic function on compact P¹ is constant. On a complex surface,
  dd^c(theta+dd^c v)=dd^c theta
for every smooth v. Therefore NONE of its smooth positive potential perturbations is Gauduchon. The same holds for eta. This is outside the bounded Gauduchon case excluded by the question.

The global nonlinear premises used from the supplied task are precisely existence and scalar uniqueness for bounded logarithmic densities in this verified admissible ordinary-reference regime, and nonemptiness of A_phi(G) for continuous G. Target solutions and all variation solutions used in the proof are constructed directly below.

3. Bounded remainder and actual non-pluripolar products

For x,z in P¹ let d_ch(x,z)² denote squared chordal distance and set
  G(x,z)=log d_ch(x,z)²+1.
Direct one-variable Poincare-Lelong calculation gives
  dd^c_x G(x,z)=delta_z-omega_1.
Its mean is zero: squared chordal distance is uniformly distributed on [0,1] under normalized sphere area, and integral_0^1 log t dt=-1.

For f=A-a, whose mean is zero, define
  w(x)=integral G(x,z)f(z)omega_1(z).
The logarithmic kernel is uniformly integrable and its translates are continuous in L¹. Therefore w is bounded continuous, with
  ||w||_infinity<=(2/e)||f||_infinity,
since integral_0^1|log t+1|dt=2/e. Distributional differentiation gives dd^c w=f omega_1 and its mean is zero. Uniqueness follows by testing a harmonic distribution against the smooth inverse Laplacian on mean-zero spherical harmonics.

As currents,
  theta+dd^c u=Omega+lambda[D]>0.
Continuity of w makes u canonical, with precisely the pole D. Its difference from phi is bounded off D, and both take value -infinity on D.

Here the weak products can be checked directly. On X minus D, u is continuous and its complex Hessian has continuous coefficients. Local mollification makes the potentials and complex Hessians converge uniformly on smaller coordinate balls. In the Bedford-Taylor recursive expression
  (dd^c f)²=dd^c(f dd^c f),
this yields the ordinary square of the continuous complex Hessian. Alternatively add a large multiple of |z|² to make the local potential bounded psh and expand back the smooth correction. Finite smooth-background corrections give the same conclusion for the nonclosed background theta. Thus the local products off D are Omega and Omega².

The non-pluripolar definition discards D. Continuous forms and their ordinary squares have coefficients absolutely continuous relative to smooth volume and give zero mass to D. Their extension from X minus D by zero is consequently the same continuous form or density on all X. Hence
  <theta+dd^c u>=Omega,
  <(theta+dd^c u)²>=Omega².
No divisorial or mixed divisorial term has been retained. This argument also applies to u+t h whenever Omega+t dd^c h stays positive.

Since Omega²=2Ab dW=c exp(F)dV, u is an actual ordinary-type solution. The supplied scalar uniqueness proves c_phi(F)=c, independently of a singular regularity theorem.

4. Product, normalization and operator constructed before the supports

The explicit rho is smooth positive, so Q is a directly defined order-zero current. The coefficient A/b depends only on the first factor, where omega_1 is already of top real degree. Therefore d((A/b)omega_1)=0 distributionally, even when A is only continuous. Uniform smooth approximation of A gives another verification. The other summand of Q is closed. Thus dQ=0 and dd^c Q=0.

Normalization is direct:
  integral rho Omega²=integral(A/a)dW=1.
Thus nu=rho Omega² is a probability with continuous positive density relative to dW, and density A/(aq) relative to dV.

For smooth h, compactness and uniform positivity give Omega+t dd^c h>0 for both signs of sufficiently small t. The genuine non-pluripolar product satisfies the exact identity
  MA_ext_theta(u+t h)
   =Omega²+2t Omega wedge dd^c h+t²(dd^c h)².
This establishes the asserted derivative. Division by the positive continuous density Omega² defines L_u. Distributional Stokes then gives
  integral L_u h dnu
   =2 integral dd^c h wedge Q
   =2<dd^c Q,h>=0.
Only continuous forms and smooth functions are multiplied here. No arbitrary distribution-times-L¹-weight product is postulated.

5. Every full supporting probability annihilates L_u

Take ANY mu in A_phi(F). For a fixed smooth h and small signed t, put
  F_t=F+log[(Omega+t dd^c h)²/Omega²].
It is continuous, and u+t h is an actual ordinary-type solution of
  MA_ext_theta(u+t h)=c exp(F_t)dV.
Scalar uniqueness therefore gives B_phi(F_t)=B_phi(F), although F_t need not satisfy the density factorization.

Uniform positivity gives, in the uniform norm,
  F_t-F=t L_u h+O(t²).
The full defining support inequality implies integral(F_t-F)dmu<=0. Divide by positive and negative t and pass to zero. Thus
  integral L_u h dmu=0
for every smooth h. The functional and supporting set have not been restricted to product densities.

6. Independent uniqueness proof for invariant probabilities

Prove the stronger result for all Borel probabilities, without assuming absolute continuity. On normalized round P¹, Delta=dd^c/omega is the standard unit-sphere Laplacian. Let e_k be real spherical harmonics on the y sphere, with e_0=1 and
  Delta_2 e_k=-lambda_k e_k.
The constants are its only zero mode; all other lambda_k are positive. Their finite span is uniformly dense in C(P¹): restrictions of polynomials decompose into spherical harmonics and are dense.

Suppose mu is a probability satisfying integral L_u h dmu=0 for every smooth h. Define signed finite measures T_k on the x sphere by
  integral f dT_k=integral f(x)e_k(y)/A(x)dmu.
Testing h=f(x)e_k(y) yields
  integral[Delta_1 f-lambda_k(A/b)f]dT_k=0
for every smooth f.

For k=0, smooth inversion of the Laplacian on mean-zero spherical harmonics shows T_0=c_0 omega_1. The x marginal is c_0 A omega_1. Probability normalization gives c_0=1/a.

For k>0, V=lambda_k A/b is continuous and strictly positive. The following lemma gives T_k=0.

Lemma. If T is a finite signed measure on the round sphere, V is continuous strictly positive, and integral(Delta f-Vf)dT=0 for every smooth f, then T=0.

Proof. Construct the sphere heat semigroup H_t by spherical harmonics: the degree-ell coefficient is multiplied by exp(-t ell(ell+1)). For t>0 the series is smooth. The maximum principle for smooth initial functions gives positivity and contraction in uniform norm. Density extends it to a strongly continuous positive contraction semigroup on continuous functions.

Choose M>=max V. The resolvent
  R_M g=integral_0^infinity exp(-Mt)H_t g dt
has norm at most 1/M and satisfies (M-Delta)R_M g=g distributionally. The equation (Delta-V)f=g is equivalent to
  f=R_M((M-V)f-g).
This is a strict contraction, with constant 1-min V/M<1. For every continuous g it produces a continuous f with Delta f=Vf+g continuous in the distributional sense. The smooth functions f_epsilon=H_epsilon f satisfy
  f_epsilon tends uniformly to f,
  Delta f_epsilon=H_epsilon(Vf+g) tends uniformly to Vf+g.
Thus (Delta-V)f_epsilon tends uniformly to g. The measure identity gives integral g dT=0 for every continuous g, proving T=0. No density or Sobolev regularity of T was assumed. End lemma.

All nonzero y modes of mu therefore vanish. Its zero mode is the marginal (A/a)omega_1. Uniform density of the harmonics and then of product test functions proves
  mu=(A/a)omega_1 wedge omega_2=nu.
Section 4 verifies that nu is invariant. Hence it is the only invariant probability.

Section 5 and the supplied nonemptiness now imply A_phi(F)={nu}. For any nonnegative measurable weight r with integral r Omega²=1 and dd^c(r Omega)=0, its product is defined because uniform positivity makes integrability relative to Omega² equivalent to integrability relative to dW. The operator identity makes r Omega² invariant. It equals nu, giving r=rho almost everywhere. This proves normalized weight uniqueness.

7. Approximation independence of the actual weighted current

Let Omega_j be any approximation in section 1. Uniform convergence to uniformly positive Omega provides uniform upper and positive lower bounds for the residual forms for sufficiently large j. Classical smooth adjoints exist uniquely up to scale, and the given normalization fixes the scale.

Write
  nu_j=rho_j Omega_j²,
  L_j h=2Omega_j wedge dd^c h/Omega_j².
Integration by parts gives integral L_j h dnu_j=0. Uniform convergence of the forms and their positive determinants gives L_j h tending uniformly to L_u h for every fixed smooth h.

Probabilities on compact X have weakly convergent subsequences. Any subsequential limit mu therefore annihilates L_u. Section 6 forces mu=nu, proving convergence of the whole sequence nu_j to nu.

This alone would not establish convergence of weighted products. For a smooth test (1,1) form xi, uniform residual control gives uniform convergence of
  f_j=(Omega_j wedge xi)/Omega_j²
 to f=(Omega wedge xi)/Omega².
Consequently
  integral rho_j Omega_j wedge xi
   =integral f_j dnu_j
   tends to integral f dnu
   =integral rho Omega wedge xi.
Thus the actual weighted currents converge to the independently defined Q.

Similarly, if q_j=Omega_j²/dW, then q_j converges uniformly to strictly positive q_0=Omega²/dW. For every continuous g,
  integral g rho_j dW
   =integral(g/q_j)dnu_j
   tends to integral(g/q_0)dnu
   =integral g rho dW.
This proves weak convergence of weights as measures, without assuming pointwise bounds or strong convergence of conformal multipliers.

The approximation class is nonempty. Approximate A uniformly by smooth positive A_j of mean a, for example with the sphere heat semigroup. Construct mean-zero w_j by the Green kernel. Smooth harmonic inversion gives smooth w_j; the Green L¹ bound gives uniform convergence to w. Then
  eta+dd^c w_j=A_j omega_1+b omega_2
converges uniformly to Omega. These are actual full-type solutions for the smooth densities F_j. The preceding independence proof also covers every nonsymmetric sequence satisfying the same residual-form hypothesis.

8. Concrete nonsmooth compact example and finite checks

Choose a=1, lambda=1/4, dV=dW, and
  t=(|Z_0|²-|Z_1|²)/(|Z_0|²+|Z_1|²),
  b=2+t,
  H=A=1/2+|t|,
  F=log(2(1/2+|t|)(2+t)).
Under omega_1, t is uniformly distributed on [-1,1], so integral A omega_1=1 and c=1. The ranges are A in [1/2,3/2] and b in [1,3]; Omega is uniformly positive. A and F are Lipschitz and not C¹ at t=0. The solution has a genuine unbounded divisorial pole and a continuous nonsmooth residual.

The reference contact radius squared is 4. With epsilon=1/2,
  epsilon theta+dd^c psi
   =(3/8)omega_1+(b/2)omega_2+(1/4)[D]>0.
All background, model, type, extra admissibility and target-solvability antecedents have been verified. Here
  rho=1/[2(2+t)],
  nu=(1/2+|t|)dW,
  dd^c theta=-2t dW is not zero.
The supporting probability is not normalized Monge-Ampere volume:
  integral Omega²=4,
  integral t dnu=0,
  integral t(Omega²/4)=5/24.

The retained symbolic program checks exact finite identities: the model's matching value and first derivative; its bounded logarithmic difference; mean A=1; Monge-Ampere mass 4; the two height moments 0 and 5/24; smoothed divisor mass 1; and the divisor probability 1/5 below. It performs no exhaustive search or numerical PDE solve and is not a proof checker.

9. Verified obstruction to unrestricted pole smoothing

In the same non-Gauduchon background take H=A=a=1, hence w=0 and u=psi. For 0<delta<=1 define
  psi_delta=lambda log[(|Z_0|²+delta|Z_1|²)/(|Z_0|²+|Z_1|²)],
  D_delta=omega_1+dd^c(psi_delta/lambda).
These potentials are globally smooth, decrease to psi as delta decreases to zero, converge in L¹, and converge smoothly away from D. D_delta is smooth positive, has integral 1, and tends to delta_p on the first factor, p={Z_0=0}. Direct differentiation gives its density
  D_delta/omega_1=4delta/[(1+delta)+(1-delta)t]².
It integrates to 1 against dt/2 and concentrates at t=-1.

The raw smooth positive forms are
  theta+dd^c psi_delta=(omega_1+lambda D_delta)+b omega_2.
Their classical normalized adjoints are explicitly
  raw rho_delta=1/[2(1+lambda)b],
  raw nu_delta=[(omega_1+lambda D_delta)/(1+lambda)] wedge omega_2.
Their weighted (1,1) forms are closed, directly verifying the adjoint equation and normalization. Hence
  raw nu_delta tends to
   [(omega_1+lambda delta_p)/(1+lambda)] wedge omega_2.
For lambda=1/4 this puts probability 1/5 on D. It cannot be any supporting probability in the admissible regime, because those are absolutely continuous with respect to smooth dV. The actual singleton probability here is dW. The weighted raw currents also retain a nonzero divisorial component, whereas Q does not.

This refutes the unrestricted assertion that arbitrary smooth positive potential approximations to an ordinary-type singular solution recover its supporting probability and weighted non-pluripolar adjoint. These raw approximations fill the pole and fail uniform residual-form convergence; their raw densities also fail uniform convergence to F. Pole smoothing can be included only with the explicit compensation removing lambda D_delta before taking the residual adjoint. That compensated residual is eta+dd^c w_j.

The theorem makes no claim for degenerate solution residuals, arbitrary singularity classes, densities outside the stated factorization, or mere bounded/capacity convergence of remainders. It does not assert potential uniqueness for every rough ordinary-type solution. It supplies an actual solution, a singleton FULL supporting set, a directly defined uniquely normalized weighted adjoint at that solution, and independence within a specified nonempty approximation class. This is the sufficient-condition alternative requested in the completion criteria.

10. Primary-source premises and reconstruction audit

Broad existence and support facts about B_phi used above are explicitly supplied mathematical premises of the problem. There are no supplied or earlier local notes used as support.

The local product premise was checked in Eric Bedford and B. A. Taylor, A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Mathematica 149 (1982), 1–40, DOI 10.1007/BF02392348. Original paper:
https://archive.ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/pacm_download/117/6320-11511_2006_Article_BF02392348.pdf
Section 2, equation (2.1), Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 are on printed page 4. They give the recursive local product and its algebraic properties and decreasing locally bounded continuity. Only the recursive product is needed here; section 3 reconstructs agreement with the continuous-form product. Their normalization differs by a constant, consistently rescaling the formulas. No theorem about arbitrary Hermitian backgrounds or rough-weight multiplication is attributed to this source.

The smooth adjoint premise was checked at a primary source by Gauduchon containing its proof:
Paul Gauduchon, Les métriques standard d'une surface complexe compacte à premier nombre de Betti pair, Astérisque 126 (1985), 129–135.
https://www.numdam.org/article/AST_1985__126__129_0.pdf
Section 3, Theorem 2, printed pages 132–133, is general compact Hermitian conformal existence and uniqueness, without the even-Betti restriction of Theorem 1. In complex dimension two it gives smooth positive rho with dd^c(rho Omega)=0, unique up to scale. Its proof identifies a one-dimensional adjoint kernel by elliptic index and maximum principle, then establishes positivity. Changing dd^c normalization leaves the zero equation unchanged. The proof page was also visually checked.

Tosatti-Weinkove's original arXiv:0910.1390v2, page 7, equation (2.15), provides an independent conformal-power normalization check:
https://arxiv.org/pdf/0910.1390
Its smooth Monge-Ampere solvability corollary is not used for singular solvability: the needed solutions are explicitly constructed. The different Gauduchon BSMF 105 (1977), 113–140 article initially located during searching does not prove this existence theorem; its introduction leaves existence unresolved, and it is not used.

The Green kernel, compact example, model envelope, special continuous-coefficient weak products, support annihilation, invariant-measure uniqueness, and weighted-current convergence were independently reconstructed above. The sphere heat-resolvent argument avoids reliance on an unverified general rough-adjoint or martingale-uniqueness theorem.
